title: A £1 million grant for young people learning AI skills.
friendlyTitle: A £1 million gift to help young people learn AI for work.
summary: On 16 November, the King's Trust and OpenAI announced a £1 million partnership to help up to 25,000 young people in the UK build AI skills for work over 18 months, with priority for those not in education, employment, or training. The Trust plans nationally recognized AI qualifications. The money is a donation to the charity, not a job offer.
friendlySummary: On 16 November, the King's Trust and OpenAI announced a £1 million partnership. Over 18 months it aims to help up to 25,000 young people in the UK learn AI skills for work, first those who are not in school, training, or a job. The Trust plans recognized AI qualifications. The money is a gift to the charity, not a job.
whyItMatters: OpenAI cites the Open University's Business Barometer 2026, which found that 68% of surveyed 16-to-24-year-olds in that group would train to improve their prospects. A skills program is not a placement. The useful check, when the courses open, is whether a recognized qualification and practice time are actually in them.
friendlyWhyItMatters: OpenAI points to an Open University survey that found 68% of young people in that group would train to improve their chances of work. A course is not a job. When the classes open, the useful question is whether they include a real qualification and time to practise.
